episodes.194014: Clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms erupted around midday and lasted through much of the afternoon.  There were some reports of wind damage and a fairly widespread area of power outages in central/northeastern Morgan county between Valhermoso Springs and southern portions of Somerville in north Alabama.
episodes.194015: Clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms erupted around midday in north Alabama and moved northward into southern middle Tennessee during the late afternoon. There were a few reports of wind damage in southern middle Tennessee.
episodes.194030: Heavy rain occurring over the course of two days fell along the eastern slopes of the Sacramento Mountains in south-central NM, estimated to have totaled three to six inches from local reports. This heavy rain collected within the normally dry Rio Penasco running eastward through southwestern Chaves County August 31st. River flooding was reported just west of the Chaves and Eddy County line, just south of U.S. Highway 82. A minor low water crossing along Cauhape Ranch Road was overtopped by peak flood waters reaching over 9 feet and well out of the banks.
episodes.194038: As a ridge of high pressure that had been centered over the central Mississippi River Valley shifted eastward toward the Southeast U.S. coastline, southerly to southeasterly flow brought sufficient moisture advection to spark the return of scattered thunderstorms across Central Alabama by August 28. High DCAPE values, in some instances over 1200-1300 J/kg, aided in downburst activity for several consecutive afternoons. Most impacted were the cities of Mountain Brook and Alexander City, both on August 29, where scattered to widespread tree and power line damage occurred. Several homes and a couple businesses sustained heavy damage in Alexander City as well.
episodes.194217: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours, and dissipated shortly after sunset. A couple of the thunderstorms were strong to severe. One storm knocked down power lines and leaned power poles in northern Madison County, resulting a power outage of about 700 residents.
episodes.194237: Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms progressed through West Virginia on August 31st as a cold front swept through the Ohio Valley. While the overall setup for severe weather was low that day, a few storms grew strong enough to produce downbursts that resulted in single tree damage across West Virginia. In addition, a few spots observed stronger intensity damaging wind gusts, which caused multiple downed trees. As the cold front inched closer to Central Appalachia, the thunderstorm threat weakened in West Virginia.
episodes.194274: Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.194357: Modest height falls as a slow moving shortwave trough crossed the region resulted in a few strong to severe storms ahead of a surface cold front. Strongest shear (25-30kts) was observed largely south of Pittsburgh allowing for more organized convection and a heightened severe threat.
episodes.194544: A slow-moving shortwave trough over New Mexico, combined with a stationary boundary across the region, developed widespread slow-moving showers and thunderstorms. Flash flooding occurred in locations where this activity trained.
episodes.194545: Slow-moving thunderstorms over the Dark Canyon Arroyo watershed led to flash flooding of some roads and low-water crossings.
episodes.195349: Thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall provided isolated flash flooding across portions of the Concho Valley and the northern Edwards Plateau.
episodes.195393: Several severe thunderstorms produced scattered wind damage from eastern West Virginia and western Maryland across northern and central Virginia.
episodes.195394: Several severe thunderstorms produced scattered wind damage from eastern West Virginia and western Maryland across northern and central Virginia.
episodes.195395: Several severe thunderstorms produced scattered wind damage from eastern West Virginia and western Maryland across northern and central Virginia.
episodes.195417: Thunderstorm activity increased during the afternoon in a warm, moist, and unstable environment. MLCAPE values were around 1500 J/kg but shear was limited. Storm activity remained sub-severe, though a brief landspout tornado was captured on video on the northeast side of Poplar Bluff.
episodes.195580: A severe thunderstorm developed over southern St. Clair County.
episodes.195585: Ahead of a cold frontal passage, clusters of showers and storms raced through southeast Ohio on the afternoon of August 31st. Convection on this particular day was not well organized, but there was enough wind to support downbursts in storms as they trekked towards the Ohio River. Main impacts on this afternoon from activity were observed from tree damage in Meigs, Jackson, Gallia, and Lawrence Counties. Storms then ventured into West Virginia for the rest of the evening.
episodes.195743: A thunderstorm moving through the Detroit River produced a wind gust just over 50 knots.
episodes.195866: An upper level low helped provide an extra source of lift which led to additional shower and thunderstorm development in the morning hours, especially over local waters, to close out the month of August. Showers and thunderstorms had been ongoing across local waters overnight and kept the activity in some areas along the immediate east coast early August 31st.
episodes.195867: With afternoon sea breezes and diurnal heating, the development of showers and thunderstorms was fueled across inland and Southwest Florida in the afternoon of August 31st. There were scattered thunderstorms across the local Gulf waters which led to hazards such as gusty winds and lightning along coastal Collier County.
episodes.195872: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed across upstate South Carolina during the afternoon into the evening. A few of the storms produced brief strong-to-damaging wind gusts. In addition, the storms tended to move slowly, and one slow-moving storm cluster produced very heavy rainfall and flash flooding in York County.
episodes.195918: Increased moisture and slow storm movement brought heavy rain and flash flooding to El Paso near Cotton Street.
episodes.195934: With Western New York in the warm sector of an approaching area of low pressure, and as a cold front approached from the west, strong thunderstorms developed in portions of the area. Timing of the storms in the morning and cloud cover limited instability for the storms to develop.
episodes.195952: The cold front that was over the region on the 29th, made limited progress eastward on the 30th. This feature continued to serve as the focus for afternoon and evening shower and thunderstorm development. A few of these storms increased to severe levels causing damaging winds which downed trees.  The storms were noted to have produced heavy downpours due to high rainfall rates, at times reaching 3 to 4 inches per hour which caused localized flash flooding in Ashe County.
episodes.195994: Showers and thunderstorms developed over the region within a warm and moist airmass on the east side of a cold front. A few of these thunderstorms increased to severe levels and produced damaging wind gusts with trees being blown down.  One line of storms developed across the northern half of Tazewell County, producing downpours at rates of three to locally five inches per hour. Crest Unit Streamflow north of the Town of Tazewell was indicating returns of between 600 and 750 cfs per mi^2, with three-hour average recurrence intervals of between 75 an 130 years.
episodes.196108: Yet another cold front impacted eastern Kentucky during the day on August 31st, rounding out the month. This time the cold front approached the state, then stalled out. Meanwhile, WPC still analyzed a surface boundary that continued eastward and through the state during the first half of the day. Then by the late afternoon hours, the actual front began to progress eastward again. This ultimately led to multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms across the region, starting with the initial boundary mid-day, and then ramping up in coverage by the afternoon hours ahead of the actual cold front. Multiple reports of severe winds and wind damage were reported across JKL's area, though Fleming, Morgan, and Johnson counties received the majority of the damage.
episodes.196222: A cold front moving through a warm and unstable air mass produced strong to severe thunderstorms over portions of Lake Superior on the 31st.
episodes.196332: A low pressure storm system moved from the northern Plains towards northeastern Canada. This placed the Lower Ohio Valley in the system's warm sector in between the system's warm and cold fronts, and with temperatures in the 90s with plenty of moisture, scattered afternoon convection developed throughout the region. A few of these storms produced isolated wind damage across central Kentucky.
episodes.200451: At the surface, an occluded low drifted northeastward across far-northwestern ON and Hudson Bay during the late afternoon of August 30th through the first couple predawn hours of the 31st. Simultaneously, the attendant warm front drifted eastward across the OH/PA border region and toward central portions of NY and PA, while the trailing cold front moved eastward from the southwestern Great Lakes and Lower MO Valley to north-central OH and the Lower to Mid OH Valley. Within the warm and moist sector between these two fronts, isolated to scattered multicell thunderstorms developed in northern OH and produced isolated straight-line convective wind damage amidst weak to moderate MUCAPE, moderate to strong DCAPE, and moderate effective bulk shear during the late afternoon through late evening.
